newsitem.title: USA: IMF set for N.Korea fact-finding mission - source.
newsitem.headline: IMF set for N.Korea fact-finding mission - source.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund holds its first talks in North Korea this month, although sources said on Monday that the Stalinist state had not launched a formal bid for IMF membership.

The sources said a fact-finding mission was expected to spend up to two weeks in Pyongyang at the invitation of the authorities there. They would talk to officials and brief them on IMF requirements if they wanted to apply to join.
"There has been no application for membership, but there has been interest in exploring the issue," one source said.

The IMF, founded after World War Two, was long regarded by Moscow and its Soviet bloc allies as an exploitative tool of the capitalist West and Pyongyang stayed on the sidelines when the former Soviet republics signed up for membership in 1992.
The IMF now has 181 member states. Cuba, North Korea and Vatican City are the best known which have not joined.
